findings.evidence: Normal disposal starts zero workers, sends compact identity pages, and retains no acquisition payload in the root ledger, but Firefox maximum 512 still fails.

Firefox passes maximum counts 64, 65, and 256 at 70, 81, and 688 ms, then reaches 6915 ms with 321 unresolved identities at 512; the combined maximum fixture also changes ID and owner-path distribution, so acquisition payload alone is no longer a sufficient causal explanation.

findings.effect: AtomVM byte counters remain unavailable; structural, identity, timing, page, callback, and inventory counters remain mandatory.
